items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name — not once in the whole call. The customer even misheard his name as 'Glen' and it went uncorrected
Never asked about stairs at origin despite the form showing a two-story home — only learned by accident that everything was from one bedroom
No special-considerations probe — long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns
No access-concerns probe at the destination storage facility — no elevator, gate hours, parking, or cart/dock question, which is the single most common time sink on a storage delivery
No 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move' — the customer's real stressor (renters arriving on the 15th) surfaced only because he volunteered it
No No Worries Damage Coverage — said 'insurance' was included in the rate but never named the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse benefit or the 60 cents per pound baseline
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip
Never explained the walk distance from truck to storage unit as a time variable
No bolded-list-at-top-of-email framing and no 'reply with any corrections'
top_strength: Outstanding room-by-room inventory discipline and a genuinely earned save. He didn't accept the 2300 sqft on the form at face value — he walked bedroom, kitchen, living, dining, garage, backyard until he established it was really a one-bedroom's worth of items, then used that to go back and re-check the 14th and hand the customer the date he'd been told was unavailable. He also priced it cleanly at both ends ($612 at three hours, $816 at four) with the 30-to-40-box 10x15 equivalent as a sense-check.
coaching_note: The mechanics were strong and the re-check on the 14th was excellent selling — but he left three differentiators on the table (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and skipped the prep speech entirely, and he never once used the customer's name. Fix the cheapest one first: get the name in the first thirty seconds and use it three times, then bolt the three differentiators onto the end of the inclusions list he already delivers well.
phone_presence_notes: Polite, competent, and clearly working the problem for the customer, but the language is transactional throughout — zero name use, few affirmations, and no rapport moment beyond the task.
